We need answer in JSON only. Need extract claims. Review: "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in.\nI love that this product was at a reasonable price and it made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out."

Need product-review semantic claims. Need choose exactly one valid primary/secondary taxonomy pair, independently determine polarity, copy evidence_span exact continuous substring from SOURCE_TEXT. No infer from star. If no supported claim empty. Need output {"claims":[...]}.

We identify claims:
1) reasonable price -> convenience_value / price_value, positive. Evidence span exact: "at a reasonable price" maybe substring. Source: "I love that this product was at a reasonable price and it made it more easy..." Exact continuous substring: "at a reasonable price" yes.
2) easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out. This relates dual_port_multi_device? Primary convenience_value secondary dual_port_multi_device. Polarity positive. Evidence: "made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out" exact substring? Source: "and it made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out." So continuous exact: "made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out" (without "it"? Let's check: "and it made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out." The substring "made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out" is present starting after "it ". Yes exact. Could also include "it made..." but fine. Claim dual port multi device. 
3) "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." This could general convenience or dual port? "Great buy" if lots USB to plug in. It implies multi-device/ports. But maybe general convenience/value. We can include? Need only supported. "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." This is a positive claim about convenience for multiple USB devices. Primary convenience_value secondary dual_port_multi_device? Or general_convenience. "lot of USB's to plug in" suggests multiple ports/devices. But evidence exact: "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." Could be dual_port_multi_device positive. But it overlaps with second. Maybe include one claim for multi-port capability from "plug two plugs in instead of just one" and one for price. The "Great buy..." maybe general recommendation not specific product claim? It does mention lot of USBs to plug in, but vague. Should we include as dual_port_multi_device positive? It says "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." That's supported about multiple USB ports. But primary topic convenience_value, secondary dual_port_multi_device. Evidence exact: "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." It includes curly apostrophe. We can include. But the instruction: "A review may contain zero or multiple claims. For every claim..." It doesn't require maximal. We can extract distinct claims. We need avoid duplicate? Could include both. However if output multiple claims, need valid. The second and third might be same aspect. But each evidence span different. Fine.

Need ensure polarity. Price positive. dual port positive. Great buy positive.

Potential "easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out" is usability? Ease of use? It says "made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out." This can be convenience_value / dual_port_multi_device, or usability_installation / ease_of_use. Which taxonomy is better? "dual_port_multi_device" exactly: ability to plug two devices, convenience. Also "ease_of_use" could be plugging. But phrase "instead of just one and keep switching it out" emphasizes dual port multi-device. Primary convenience_value. Good.

Could there be compatibility? No.

Need output no markdown, exact schema.

Let's craft JSON:
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "primary_topic": "convenience_value",
      "secondary_topic": "price_value",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "evidence_span": "at a reasonable price"
    },
    {
      "primary_topic": "convenience_value",
      "secondary_topic": "dual_port_multi_device",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "evidence_span": "made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out"
    },
    {
      "primary_topic": "convenience_value",
      "secondary_topic": "dual_port_multi_device",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "evidence_span": "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in."
    }
  ]
}

Need verify evidence span exact continuous substring. "at a reasonable price" appears exactly? Source: "I love that this product was at a reasonable price and it made..." yes. "made it more easy..." Source: "and it made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out." The substring begins "made it more easy..." yes. "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." Source first line exactly has curly apostrophe? User source: "Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in." It uses ’ in USB’s. Yes. Include period. Good. 
Need maybe no "I love that this product was" not needed.

Should we include the price claim evidence "reasonable price" and polarity positive. Yes.

Could "it made it more easy..." grammar, exact. Good.

No additional fields. Ensure JSON valid with curly apostrophe. Yes.

Need final only JSON.

{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"convenience_value","secondary_topic":"price_value","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"at a reasonable price"},{"primary_topic":"convenience_value","secondary_topic":"dual_port_multi_device","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"made it more easy to plug two plugs in instead of just one and keep switching it out"},{"primary_topic":"convenience_value","secondary_topic":"dual_port_multi_device","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"Great buy if you got a lot of USB’s to plug in."}]}
